messages.content: Find me all the classical concerts near Berlin and Paris happening next Friday, and I am interested only in those with available parking.

function.name: concert_find_nearby
function.description: Locate nearby concerts based on specific criteria like genre and availability of parking. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

location.description: The city where the user wants to find a concert.

date.description: The date on which the user wants to attend a concert.

genre.description: The genre of music of the concert.

We need to call the function concert_find_nearby twice: one for Berlin, one for Paris. The date is next Friday. We need to compute next Friday's date. Today is 2026-10-09. Let's calculate next Friday. 2026-10-09 is a Thursday? Let's check: 2026-10-09. 2026-10-01 was a Sunday? Actually let's compute: 2026-10-09. 2026-10-01 is Sunday? Let's quickly approximate: 2026-01-01 is a Monday? Actually 2026-01-01 is a Monday? Let's not rely on memory. Instead we can compute using known reference: 2025-12-31 is Thursday? Wait 2025-12-31 is Thursday? Let's compute: 2025-01-01 is Wednesday? Actually 2025-01-01 is Wednesday? Let's compute: 2024-01-01 is Monday (2024 is leap year). 2024-01-01 Monday. 2024 has 366 days, so 2025-01-01 is Wednesday (Monday + 2). 2025-01-01 Wednesday. 2025-12-31 is Wednesday? 2025 has 365 days, so 2025-12-31 is Wednesday + 364 mod 7 = Wednesday + 0 = Wednesday. So 2025-12-31 Wednesday. Then 2026-01-01 is Thursday. So 2026-01-01 Thursday. 2026-10-09: Let's compute days from Jan 1 to Oct 9. 2026 is not leap year. Days per month: Jan 31, Feb 28, Mar 31, Apr 30, May 31, Jun 30, Jul 31, Aug 31, Sep 30, Oct 9 days. Sum: 31+28=59, +31=90, +30=120, +31=151, +30=181, +31=212, +31=243, +30=273, +9=282. So 282 days after Jan 1. Jan 1 is day 1. So day 282 corresponds to Oct 9. Now day of week: Jan 1 is Thursday. Add 281 days (since Jan 1 is day 1). 281 mod 7 = 281 - 280 = 1. So day 282 is Thursday + 1 = Friday. So Oct 9, 2026 is Friday. Wait but we computed earlier that Oct 9 is Friday. That means today is Friday. But the user says "next Friday". If today is Friday, next Friday would be Oct 16, 2026. So date should be 2026-10-16. So we need to call function with date "2026-10-16".

We also need to specify genre "Classical" and amenities "Parking". The function signature: location, date, genre, amenities? default: ["Parking"]. So we can pass amenities: "Parking" or array? The type says amenities?: "Parking" | "Food and Beverages" | "VIP Seating" | "Disability Access"[], default: ["Parking"]. It seems ambiguous: maybe it's an array of strings. We'll pass ["Parking"].

Thus two calls:

concert_find_nearby({"location":"Berlin","date":"2026-10-16","genre":"Classical","amenities":["Parking"]})

and same for Paris.

We need to output results. We'll call function twice.
